Facelifted 2028 Mercedes SL Roadster To Gain Benz Line
20 photos
Photo: Mercedes-AMG
The Mercedes-Benz SL will return in 2027, joining the facelifted AMG and Maybach lines. Giving the canvas-topped roadster a third personality makes plenty of sense. Rather than chasing aggressive performance or extravagant luxury, the Benz would put greater emphasis on relaxed open-top motoring.
None other than chief executive officer Ola Kallenius provided the confirmation, and he did so during the Golden Steering Wheel awards ceremony in Berlin. Speaking to Auto Bild, the big kahuna also posed for a photograph that included a camouflaged example of the 2028 Mercedes-Benz SL.
The German automaker's three-pointed star dominates the front grille, and this badge is flanked by star-motif running lights in the headlights. A cleaner front bumper design hides under the camo wrap, giving the Benz a distinct visual identity from the Panamericana-grilled AMG or the ultra-lux Maybach with its monolithic grille design and look-at-me wheel choices.
Kallenius explained that Merc is giving each SL version a distinct purpose, with the Benz combining improved comfort with the roof down, a more balanced relationship between sporting ability and refinement, and timeless styling. With the 2028 model year, the SL is also expected to drop the poor-selling turbo inline-four engine that currently powers the AMG SL 43.
The 43 also happens to be Mercedes-AMG's only rear-drive SL as of this writing. At the end of the day, Formula 1 powertrain technologies don't matter too much when you're getting a puny 2.0-liter mill for a simply ridiculous 126,686.45 euros. That kind of money can get you much nicer or more performance-oriented vehicles, for sure!
Photo: Mercedes-AMG Opting for the 55 results in the M177 twin-turbo V8, whereas the 63 offers a bit more oomph from said 4.0-liter unit. And finally, the 63 with plug-in hybrid assistance offers a tremendous 805 horsepower and 1,047 pound-feet (1,420 Newton-meters) of twist.
Unfortunately, the plug-in part of the powertrain was not designed with electric range in mind. That's why the SL 63 S E PERFORMANCE can't do better than 13 kilometers in the WLTP, a figure that can be alternatively interpreted as 8 miles. The Maybach line is only available in 680 specification, which uses the aforementioned cross-plane V8.
This lump develops a respectable 585 ps (577 hp) and 800 Nm (590 lb-ft) between 2,500 and 5,000 rpm. Come 2027, all V8 options are likely to be replaced by the M177 Evo flat-plane V8. The switch from a cross- to a flat-plane crankshaft results in a different soundtrack, but Mercedes and the AMG division also decided on it due to emission regulations.
While a CPC fires two cylinders consecutively on the same bank, the FPC alternates firing evenly between the left and right cylinder banks of a V-type engine, thus creating the more exotic sounds we associate with flat-plane mills. The alternating exhaust pulses happen to eliminate exhaust gas interference between cylinders, allowing the hot-V turbos to spool more cleanly.
Speaking of cleanly, the M177 Evo runs the Miller cycle to maintain a stoichiometric air-fuel ratio under high load. While a V8 engine is plausible for the Benz SL, an I6 would suit its character much better. After all, the original 300 SL from the 1950s came with a straight-six mill. The 3.0-liter engine of the CLE 53 is a great candidate, with AMG claiming 443 horsepower and either 413 or 443 pound-feet (560 or 600 Newton-meters) with overboost active.
